headline: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to a public fund
dek: The fund still needs shareholder approval and can grow as the company's valuation rises.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A public benefit fund
body: Anthropic announced the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, which will hold 5% of the company's shares (Anthropic, TechCrunch).
The move still needs shareholder approval, according to Anthropic.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the fund can grow
s3.body: According to Anthropic and TechCrunch, the design allows:

points.t: A 50% rise in valuation above a baseline (Anthropic).
The board can add 2 percentage points in shares (Anthropic).
A wholly-owned LLC of the company, Anthropic says.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: What the fund is for
body: According to Anthropic, it covers what does not fit inside the company, such as large donations to nonprofits or direct distributions to specific groups.
One cited focus is AI's labor-market impact, which already got $200 million in research, Anthropic says.

stat.cap: of shares go to the fund, Anthropic says

items.t: Anthropic says it will detail governance in the coming months.
The valuation milestones will also be detailed, the company says.
The company promises a report on progress against its mission.

caption.hook: Anthropic will put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund.
body: According to Anthropic, confirmed by TechCrunch, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will hold 5% of the shares, pending shareholder approval. For every 50% rise in valuation above a baseline, the board can add another 2 percentage points.

The company says the fund is for large donations to nonprofits and direct distributions to specific groups, such as people affected by AI in the labor market. It also says none of the fund's shares will go to lobbying or political giving. Governance and milestones will be detailed in the coming months.
